summary: ISO-NE and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee jointly ask FERC to hold the E-11 show cause proceeding in abeyance for 90 days from August 17, 2026 and commit to a single section 205 filing by November 16, 2026.
ask: Hold the proceeding in abeyance for 90 days starting August 17, 2026, with a five-day comment period and a ruling by August 13, 2026.

points.point: The movants commit to file by November 16, 2026.
points.quote: ISO-NE and the PTOs will submit the FPA Section 205 filing to the Commission on or before November 16, 2026.

points.point: They ask for a shortened comment period and expedited ruling because the response is due August 17.
points.quote: respectfully request that the Commission shorten the comment period for this motion to five days and grant expedited treatment

points.point: They say more time is needed to develop proposals and present them for stakeholder review.
points.quote: additional time is needed to develop those proposals and present them for stakeholder review.

points.point: The filing will cover all five reform categories: study processes, cost transparency, co-location rules, flexible load service and generation studies.
points.quote: efficient study processes, cost transparency, co-location rules, flexible load service, and generation studies

points.point: Study reform will include a large load definition with a size and interconnection voltage threshold, and evaluation of alternative transmission technologies.
points.quote: This definition will be based on the characteristics of ISO-NE’s transmission system and will include load size and an interconnection voltage threshold.

throughLine.text: Uses the abeyance option in the E-11 order to postpone the 60-day deadline and maps ISO-NE's planned section 205 filing onto the order's five reform categories.

figures.label: Requested abeyance period
figures.quote: hold the Section 206 proceeding initiated by the Show Cause Order in abeyance for 90 days
